class="ClampContent-hcSZcW llFVIv"><div class="BaseWrap-sc-gzmcOU BaseText-eqOrNE UnifiedProductCardDescriptionWrapper-dyAmCu deqABF fxYvgV jaKDYU"><div><p>There aren’t any obvious big differences between the original and updated versions of Ooni’s <a href="https://www.wired.com/review/ooni-karu-16/" target="_blank">best-selling multifuel oven</a>. The Karu 2 is still light and portable, a mere 33.7 pounds, which makes it easy to move around your backyard and assemble. The powder-coated finish over a stainless steel shell still achieves the remarkable feat of concentrating heat without a ton of heavy, dense insulation. You can still use either charcoal or wood or buy an optional <a data-offer-url="https://ooni.com/products/ooni-gas-burner" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">gas burner ($120)</a>.</p><p>But while the upgrades are small, they&#x27;re very much appreciated. The fuel tray is 45 percent bigger, which means you can buy larger fuel sticks than <a data-offer-url="https://ooni.com/collections/shop-all/products/ooni-premium-assorted-oak-pack" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://ooni.com/collections/shop-all/products/ooni-premium-assorted-oak-pack&quot;}" href="https://ooni.com/collections/shop-all/products/ooni-premium-assorted-oak-pack" rel="nofollow" target="_blank">Ooni’s proprietary ones</a>—I found pecan and cherry logs that fit in the burner at my local hardware store. Bigger pieces of wood mean you no longer have to stoke the flames to maintain heat, like a coal shoveler on a WWII-era steamship. The bigger tray also means the pizza stone heats more evenly. I got it up to 750 degrees within 20 minutes and verified that the temperature varied only a few degrees from edge to edge.</p><p>There is also a new ClearView technology to keep that all-important glass door from getting smoked up and smudgy. It’s been several weeks of use, and I have yet to get the door dirty. If you really want to achieve the top high temp of 950 degrees Fahrenheit, I would suggest getting the burner: Past 750 degrees, the temperature is a little hard to maintain. If you need a little more space, it also comes in <a data-offer-url="https://ooni.com/products/ooni-karu-2-pro" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://ooni.com/products/ooni-karu-2-pro&quot;}" href="https://ooni.com/products/ooni-karu-2-pro" rel="nofollow" target="_blank">a 16-inch Karu 2 Pro size</a>. This is still the most gorgeous, versatile, portable backyard pizza oven for your money. UnifiedProductCardDescriptionWrapper-dyAmCu deqABF fxYvgV jaKDYU"><div><p>At a low cost, the <a href="https://www.wired.com/review/gourmia-all-in-one-pizza-oven/" target="_blank">Gourmia All-in-One</a> offers a few lovely qualities. It plugs into a regular outlet, can be used indoors, and crests 750 degrees Fahrenheit in 20 or 25 minutes. It also offers individual control over the top and bottom heating elements, so you can adjust if your cheese isn&#x27;t melty enough or your bottom not quite cooked. Pizzas baked on this oven came out quite well, with a leopard-spotted bottom, a bubbly cheese topping, and a lovely puffy crust.</p><p>It&#x27;s also, technically, an air fryer and a conventional oven. But caveats are in order. The heating can be wonky and uneven, and there&#x27;s an awful lot of heat loss through the door. If you preheat the stone, your pizza will come out well. But it&#x27;s not a top-line <a href="https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-toaster-ovens/" target="_blank">toaster oven</a> or <a href="https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-air-fryer/" target="_blank">air fryer</a> without the thermal mass of the stone keeping things even. class="BaseWrap-sc-gzmcOU BaseText-eqOrNE UnifiedProductCardDescriptionWrapper-dyAmCu deqABF fxYvgV jaKDYU"><div><p>I&#x27;ve been dreaming of building a backyard firepit for decades, having been inspired by my late father&#x27;s stories of taking his mom&#x27;s pies down to bake in <a data-offer-url="https://sparklemarkets.wordpress.com/2017/01/13/the-tale-of-brier-hill-pizza/" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://sparklemarkets.wordpress.com/2017/01/13/the-tale-of-brier-hill-pizza/&quot;}" href="https://sparklemarkets.wordpress.com/2017/01/13/the-tale-of-brier-hill-pizza/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank">the neighborhood’s community pizza ovens</a>. I&#x27;ve owned three Ooni ovens (one as an <a data-offer-url="https://ooni.com/blogs/news/uuni-becomes-ooni-faq" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">Uuni</a>) but always wanted to cook on live fire, wood-burning fire pit instead of pellets or gas. The Breeo finally made that dream come true. The base Breeo is a heavy-duty <a href="https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-fire-pits/" target="_blank">competitor to the better-known Solo Stove fire pit</a>. I love the stylish Corten steel, which I treated to speed the weathering process, but what really separates it is the assortment of available accessories, headlined by a well-designed pizza oven that sits on top and turns the pit into a wood-fired pizza oven. I&#x27;ve made about a dozen pies on the Breeo and had mostly good results, though it is important to read the temperature of the deck and spritz it with water if it has gotten too hot, as real logs will reach temps little wood pellets won&#x27;t. Master the quirks (all backyard pizza ovens have quirks) and you&#x27;ll be rewarded with quick cooks and true char. Ooni has a new gas management technology that keeps the temperature consistent across the huge surface. However, it&#x27;s a <em>lot</em> of gas line and a lot of fuel. Even just waiting for the propane to fill so I could light the oven took a really long time.</p><p>With such a big opening and no door, heat <em>pours</em> out of this thing. You can feel it from several feet away, which means it&#x27;s not ideal for smaller patios. However, the temperatures are remarkably consistent across the cooking surface, and the new digital temperature hub checks the heat at multiple points throughout the oven. You can even connect it to Ooni&#x27;s new app (<a data-offer-url="https://apps.apple.com/us/app/ooni-pizza-ovens/id1043854726" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">iOS</a>, <a data-offer-url="https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ooni.app&amp;hl=en_US" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">Android</a>) to monitor the heat remotely, although I get a little nervous stepping away from an oven that is burning at 900 degrees Fahrenheit. You can control each side independently, so you can either cook multiple pizzas at a time or just push some broccoli in next to your steak. The price includes two food probes, but oddly enough, no pizza peel. —<em>Adrienne So</em></p><table><thead><tr><th>Specs</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>Fuel:</strong> Gas | <strong>Dimensions:</strong> 31 x 28 x 17 inches | <strong>Material:</strong> Powder-coated carbon steel | <strong>Pie size:</strong> 20-inch pies</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div><div class="UnifiedProductCardReviewSection-ekgYes cJDFYa"></div></div></div></div></div></li></ul></div></div></div></div></div><div class="LazyChunk-kMbfxl kVoYsH"><div data-testid="RowWrapper" class="BaseWrap-sc-gzmcOU RowWrapper-EQDhp deqABF fWZsjA GalleryPageChunkRow-eInvyO jdunEg"><div class="GridWrapper-cFSKbf kfCuhH grid grid-margins grid-items-2 grid-layout--adrail narrow" data-journey-hook="grid-wrapper"><div class="GridItem-beYvyV kCPYUp grid--item grid-layout__content"><div class=""><ul class="GalleryPageSlides-hsMHHj jNtgjz"><li class="gallery__slides__slide" id="6830c3ff580e653dfbee45af"><div><div class="UnifiedProductCardBody-hIYvDT cYxZHF product-embed impressionTracking" data-item="{&quot;ctaAnalyticsName&quot;:&quot;buy-button-click&quot;,&quot;bookmarkMeta&quot;:{&quot;slug&quot;:&quot;gallery/best-backyard-pizza-oven&quot;,&quot;title&quot;:&quot;The Best Pizza Ovens to Make the Perfect Slice&quot;},&quot;brand&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Cuisinart&quot;},&quot;contentType&quot;:&quot;product&quot;,&quot;ctaHref&quot;:null,&quot;dangerousCredit&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;dangerousHed&quot;:&quot;Best Grilltop Pizza Oven&quot;,&quot;dek&quot;:[&quot;div&quot;,[&quot;p&quot;,&quot;Technically, you can turn any lidded grill into a pizza oven, as long as you&#x27;ve got the right size pizza stone and a good mounting bracket. And when you&#x27;re not making pizza you can cook burgers or hot dogs on a powerful propane grill, or griddle a few pancakes on the side griddle: It&#x27;s an American quadfecta. GalleryPageIntroBody-jXgcYV hmxIrG" data-journey-hook="client-content" data-testid="BodyWrapper"><div><h2></h2><div name="accordion" class="AccordionWrapper-hsYVHT bgMFty"><div class="AccordionItemWrapper-eWlGuu eNwKZf"><div class="AccordionContainer-foSklP iRHdCZ"><div data-testid="accordion-item-container" class="AccordionItemContainer-ywYcO eQgPvY"><div class="AccordionItemContainerLabel-ioTxOM diANax"><p>Who We Are and How We Tested</p></div><button class="BaseButton-lbLhfD ButtonWrapper-igqDZ gTIqfM hKIiJv button button--utility AccordionItemContainerButton-eSsfaw Wvvyo" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;Button&quot;}" data-testid="Button" role="button" type="button"><span class="ButtonLabel-cyWivE hvohFn button__label">AccordionItemContainerButton</span><div class="ButtonIconWrapper-gzKJtq bQqPLN button__icon-container"><svg class="ButtonIcon-bdIQNJ jKYSoZ button-icon icon icon-large-chevron" focusable="false" width="32" height="32" viewBox="0 0 32 32" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><title>LargeChevron</title><path fill-rule="evenodd" clip-rule="evenodd" d="m1.47 10.53 1.06-1.06L16 22.94 29.47 9.47l1.06 1.06L16 25.06 1.47 10.53Z" fill="#000"></path></svg></div></button></div><div class="AccordionItemContainerContent-bPelIb leTzLN opening-animation"><div><p>WIRED reviewer Adrienne So has tested many pizza ovens and made more than a thousand pizzas over <a href="https://www.wired.com/review/review-uuni-pro/" target="_blank">the past seven years.</a> WIRED reviewer Matthew Korfhage is a longtime food writer who&#x27;s written about pizza on both coasts over 15 years, from <a data-offer-url="https://www.wweek.com/portland/article-24233-cheap-eats-2015-pizza.html" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://www.wweek.com/portland/article-24233-cheap-eats-2015-pizza.html&quot;}" href="https://www.wweek.com/portland/article-24233-cheap-eats-2015-pizza.html" rel="nofollow" target="_blank">sausage slices in Portland</a> to <a data-offer-url="https://www.delawareonline.com/story/life/food/2023/10/02/how-mexican-pizza-became-a-distinctly-philadelphia-food/70825599007/" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://www.delawareonline.com/story/life/food/2023/10/02/how-mexican-pizza-became-a-distinctly-philadelphia-food/70825599007/&quot;}" href="https://www.delawareonline.com/story/life/food/2023/10/02/how-mexican-pizza-became-a-distinctly-philadelphia-food/70825599007/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank">the story of Mexican pizza in Philadelphia</a>.</p><p>We test each pizza oven over the course of a few weeks, using homemade dough (Adrienne likes <a data-offer-url="https://ooni.com/blogs/recipes/classic-pizza-dough" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">Ooni&#x27;s classic pizza dough recipe</a>), fresh dough balls procured from local pizzerias, store-bought fresh dough, and frozen pizzas. We use infrared thermometers to make sure the temperature of the cooking surface is consistent (and is what the built-in thermometer says it is). Where relevant, we also cross-check built-in thermometers on each oven against our own ambient thermometers.</p><p>Pizza ovens are also quite a bit more versatile than you might think. Over years of testing, Adrienne has used her pizza ovens to sear steaks, quick-cook salmon, and pan-fry broccoli. Matthew has air fried wings in a pizza oven, grilled pork chops, charred asparagus, and blackened chicken.</p></div></div></div></div><div class="AccordionItemWrapper-eWlGuu eNwKZf"><div class="AccordionContainer-foSklP iRHdCZ"><div data-testid="accordion-item-container" class="AccordionItemContainer-ywYcO eQgPvY"><div class="AccordionItemContainerLabel-ioTxOM diANax"><p>Pizza Baking Tips</p></div><button class="BaseButton-lbLhfD ButtonWrapper-igqDZ gTIqfM hKIiJv button button--utility AccordionItemContainerButton-eSsfaw Wvvyo" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;Button&quot;}" data-testid="Button" role="button" type="button"><span class="ButtonLabel-cyWivE hvohFn button__label">AccordionItemContainerButton</span><div class="ButtonIconWrapper-gzKJtq bQqPLN button__icon-container"><svg class="ButtonIcon-bdIQNJ jKYSoZ button-icon icon icon-large-chevron" focusable="false" width="32" height="32" viewBox="0 0 32 32" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><title>LargeChevron</title><path fill-rule="evenodd" clip-rule="evenodd" d="m1.47 10.53 1.06-1.06L16 22.94 29.47 9.47l1.06 1.06L16 25.06 1.47 10.53Z" fill="#000"></path></svg></div></button></div><div class="AccordionItemContainerContent-bPelIb leTzLN opening-animation"><div><p>It&#x27;s taken me many years, and many thousands of pizzas, to refine my pizza-making technique. And to be honest, my Neapolitan-style pizzas don&#x27;t really meet the standard set by the <a data-offer-url="https://www.pizzanapoletana.org/en/" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana</a>, the world authority on Neapolitan pizzas. (Ooni pizza ovens, including previous models of our top-rated Karu 2, are the only models we recommend that the AVPN has also recommended.)</p><p>But over the years, I have accumulated a few tips for those of you who find making a pizza to be a little bit awkward or intimidating. If you&#x27;ve refrigerated your dough, bring it to room temperature first. Sprinkle flour or cornmeal generously on the peel before you assemble your pizza. Be patient and stretch it from the inside out. It is cheating, but I also am guilty of using <a data-offer-url="https://www.amazon.com/GOBAM-Bamboo-Wood-Rolling-Small/dp/B0721BQ2YP/" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank" data-aps-asin="B0721BQ2YP" data-aps-asc-tag="w050b-20">a tiny rolling pin ($10)</a> to help me get the dough as thin as possible.</p><p>An authentic Neapolitan pie will use a few specific ingredients. When you&#x27;re making your own dough, reach for <a data-offer-url="https://www.amazon.com/Antimo-Caputo-Chefs-Flour-Kilo/dp/B07144K4T6/ref=sr_1_3" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank" data-aps-asin="B07144K4T6" data-aps-asc-tag="w050b-20">00 flour</a>, which is milled specifically for pizza and pasta. Fresh mozzarella will make your pizza damp, so I use a mix of fresh and shredded, low-moisture cheese for the cheesiest, meltiest pie. If you&#x27;re not sticking to a strictly Neapolitan recipe, we also have a few favorite pies we&#x27;d like to recommend. Cizmar and I like a good Buffalo pie with <a data-offer-url="https://www.amazon.com/Franks-RedHot-Original-Cayenne-Pepper/dp/B000XGGX6G/" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank" data-aps-asin="B000XGGX6G" data-aps-asc-tag="w050b-20">Frank&#x27;s Red Hot</a> and <a data-offer-url="https://www.amazon.com/stores/page/F5EA56D9-D3C1-493D-AB64-8A3FAEB3258C" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">pickles</a>. I also recently tried <a data-offer-url="https://brightland.co/products/pizza-oil" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">Brightland&#x27;s Pizza Oil</a> in a squeeze bottle; while it&#x27;s good as a finishing sauce to drizzle over pies, you could make your own for much cheaper by putting olive oil and herbs in a <a data-offer-url="https://www.restaurantware.com/smallwares/kitchen-tools/squeeze-bottles/8-oz-clear-plastic-squeeze-bottle-precision-tip-2-x-2-x-7-1-count-box/" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">squeeze bottle</a>.</p><p>Pizza ovens are more versatile than you might think: I cook everything from salmon to steak to chicken thighs in mine by preheating <a href="https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-cast-iron-pans/">a cast iron pan</a> in a hot oven and popping the food right in. For more guidance, Ooni has <a data-offer-url="https://ooni.com/products/ooni-cooking-with-fire-cookbook" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">a cookbook</a>; <a data-offer-url="https://www.amazon.com/Finding-Fire-Cooking-most-elemental/dp/174379732X?tag=w050b-20" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank" data-aps-asin="174379732X" data-aps-asc-tag="w050b-20">chef Francis Mallman&#x27;s books</a> are also a good source of inspiration. —<em>Adrienne So</em></p></div></div></div></div><div class="AccordionItemWrapper-eWlGuu eNwKZf"><div class="AccordionContainer-foSklP iRHdCZ"><div data-testid="accordion-item-container" class="AccordionItemContainer-ywYcO eQgPvY"><div class="AccordionItemContainerLabel-ioTxOM diANax"><p>Make Your Own Oven</p></div><button class="BaseButton-lbLhfD ButtonWrapper-igqDZ gTIqfM hKIiJv button button--utility AccordionItemContainerButton-eSsfaw Wvvyo" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;Button&quot;}" data-testid="Button" role="button" type="button"><span class="ButtonLabel-cyWivE hvohFn button__label">AccordionItemContainerButton</span><div class="ButtonIconWrapper-gzKJtq bQqPLN button__icon-container"><svg class="ButtonIcon-bdIQNJ jKYSoZ button-icon icon icon-large-chevron" focusable="false" width="32" height="32" viewBox="0 0 32 32" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><title>LargeChevron</title><path fill-rule="evenodd" clip-rule="evenodd" d="m1.47 10.53 1.06-1.06L16 22.94 29.47 9.47l1.06 1.06L16 25.06 1.47 10.53Z" fill="#000"></path></svg></div></button></div><div class="AccordionItemContainerContent-bPelIb leTzLN opening-animation"><div><p>Is your patio already occupied by a giant Traeger? Your grill or smoker probably has a pizza attachment that you can buy for less than a new oven. Senior director Martin Cizmar&#x27;s favorite is the Yoder Smoker <a data-offer-url="https://indigopoolpatiobbq.com/products/yoder-smokers-wood-fired-oven" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">wood-fired oven attachment ($499)</a>, which has saved him from many a night of pellet fire flameouts. It sits under the smoker’s hood, atop a steel sheet that sits over the firebox. The sheet is a diffuser and has holes of increasing size as you move away from the fire so that the section farthest from the flame gets more exposure. The design provides a consistent temperature along the oven’s floor, and it works well, with the farthest corners of the oven still cresting 650 degrees Fahrenheit.</p><p>You can also turn your normal, indoor oven into a pizza oven. While most ovens max out at 500 degrees Fahrenheit, one way to impart more heat to your pizza is by pre-heating a baking surface with a high thermal mass—which will maintain temperature stability and directly deliver its stored-up heat energy. An easy way to do this is by pre-heating a <a href="https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-cast-iron-pans/">cast-iron pan</a> or <a data-offer-url="https://www.williams-sonoma.com/products/williams-sonoma-pizza-steel/" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">baking steel</a>. A classic <a data-offer-url="https://www.amazon.com/LloydPans-Kitchenware-Detroit-Style-Pizza/dp/B01FY5PHIK?th=1" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank" data-aps-asin="B01FY5PHIK" data-aps-asc-tag="w050b-20">Lloyd pan</a> is one preferred tool for Detroit- or Sicilian-style pan pizza, which work well in conventional ovens.</p><p>Several of our favorite grill and pizza oven manufacturers, like <a data-offer-url="https://www.kamadojoe.com/collections/accessories/products/kamado-joe-ceramic-pizza-stone" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">Kamado</a> and <a data-offer-url="https://www.acehardware.com/departments/outdoor-living/grills-and-smokers/grill-cooking-accessories/8267239" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">Weber</a>, also make ceramic pizza stones. Check out our guide to the <a data-offer-url="https://www.wired.com/story/best-portable-grills/" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">Best Portable Grills</a> and <a data-offer-url="https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-grilling-accessories-tools/" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">Grill Accessories</a> for more.</p></div></div></div></div></div><h2></h2><h2>Honorable Mentions</h2><p>We&#x27;ve tried a lot of pizza ovens. The optional woodbox was oppressively difficult to use, for those who want the ability to cook with fire. But the Gozney&#x27;s price, previously among the most expensive entrants, now seems pretty reasonable.</p><native-ad position="in-content" shouldDisplayLabel="true"></native-ad><p><strong><a data-offer-url="https://www.amazon.com/Ninja-OO101-Technology-Resistant-Terracotta/dp/B0C6BQVDX3" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank" data-aps-asin="B0C6BQVDX3" data-aps-asc-tag="w050b-20">Ninja Wood-Fired Oven for $300</a>:</strong> If you&#x27;re looking for a remarkably sturdy and versatile outdoor oven, this is <a href="https://www.wired.com/review/ninja-outdoor-woodfire-oven/">a pretty good pick</a> with a top temperature of 700 degrees. The door is a little sticky which makes baking pizza at high heat a little tricky, but if you want one device that can do everything from smoke a pork shoulder to make muffins to bake a pizza pie, this is your pick.</p><ad position="mid-content"></ad><p><a data-offer-url="https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CHCP9PSN/" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank" data-aps-asin="B0CHCP9PSN" data-aps-asc-tag="w050b-20"><strong>The Piezano for $99</strong>:</a> This <a data-offer-url="https://www.tiktok.com/discover/piezano-pizza-oven" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://www.tiktok.com/discover/piezano-pizza-oven&quot;}" href="https://www.tiktok.com/discover/piezano-pizza-oven" rel="nofollow" target="_blank">TikTok-popular</a> oven is affordable, small, and convenient. It looks a little like a <a href="https://www.wired.com/story/waffle-maker-rants-and-raves/">waffle iron</a>, and comes with <a data-offer-url="https://granitestone.com/products/granitestone-piezano-replacement-wood-pizza-peels" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">handy double paddles</a> for easier placement. Astonishingly, its claims of heating the top and bottom elements to 800 degrees Fahrenheit are accurate, and it takes about 15 minutes, which allows for short cook times. But note the heating element at the top doesn&#x27;t cover the whole surface area, so you have to rotate your pies pretty frequently. Also, opening the top like a waffle maker means that it doesn&#x27;t retain heat very well. It dropped by 100 to 200 degrees between pies and requires a bit of recovery time.</p><h2>Also Tested</h2><figure class="AssetEmbedWrapper-fkZDUs kHRAYC asset-embed"><div data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank"><strong>Current Backyard Model P for $699</strong>:</a> No less a TV food personage than Alton Brown has signed on as an endorser of this 1,750-watt electric indoor/outdoor pizza oven, which will heat to 850 degrees Fahrenheit using a standard power outlet. Heat is relatively even across the oven, and it&#x27;ll get up to top temp in around 30 minutes. But cook settings are constrained to a few preset levels (New-York style, thin crust, Neapolitan, frozen), whose temps and cooking times can be a bit fussy to fiddle with. At least during early months, the app and on-device controls tend to offer more quirks than functionality. Display temp and actual temp don&#x27;t always match, and its top thermal elements turn on and off like the lights in a David Lynch movie, according to what the company calls a proprietary algorithm. Still, you can make a great pizza on this thing, and you can make it indoors. Current says it plans to add more functions and cooking modes in future updates, and we&#x27;ll keep testing. But it feels less than fully baked at the moment, especially at its price.</p><ad position="mid-content"></ad><p><strong><a data-offer-url="https://www.surlatable.com/product/pizzaque-r-outdoor-pizza-oven/6869978" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">Pizzacraft Pizzaque for $130</a>:</strong> This oven is adorable and affordable, and you can stand it in your driveway and cook a good pizza while sitting in your camp chair. However, it just doesn&#x27;t get as hot or cook as evenly as a better-insulated oven does.</p><h2>The Best Accessories</h2><p>Some pizza ovens provide you with proprietary accessories to set you on your pizza path. But we&#x27;ve also found a few extras to be helpful along the way:</p><p><strong><a data-offer-url="https://www.amazon.com/Ooni-Plastic-Infrared-Thermometer-7-5/dp/B07RWCRVS5/" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank" data-aps-asin="B07RWCRVS5" data-aps-asc-tag="w050b-20">A handheld infrared thermometer for $47</a>:</strong> Even if the oven has a built-in thermometer, a handheld infrared thermometer is a great way to check the temperature on different areas of the pizza stone. It&#x27;s also important to make sure the stone has time to reheat after each pizza.</p><p><strong><a data-offer-url="https://www.amazon.com/New-Star-Foodservice-50295-Wooden/dp/B009LPDNPO?tag=w050b-20" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank" data-aps-asin="B009LPDNPO" data-aps-asc-tag="w050b-20">A wooden pizza peel for $34</a>:</strong> If you own multiple peels, it&#x27;s quick and easy to prep one pizza while another is baking. WIRED reviewers Adrienne So and Matthew Korfhage each own several peels, including a <a data-offer-url="https://ooni.com/products/ooni-pizza-turning-peel" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">useful small turning peel</a>. But for launching, the dough is much less likely to stick on a wooden peel, especially if you first sprinkle on some semolina or flour.</p><p><strong><a data-offer-url="https://www.amazon.com/Lodge-Skillet-Pre-Seasoned-Skillet-Stovetop/dp/B00006JSUA?tag=w050b-20" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank" data-aps-asin="B00006JSUA" data-aps-asc-tag="w050b-20">A cast-iron skillet for $25</a>:</strong> You can also use a cast-iron pan in your pizza oven to sear steaks or pan-roast broccoli. Lodge&#x27;s pans <a href="https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-cast-iron-pans/">work just as well</a> as much more expensive options.</p><p><strong><a data-offer-url="https://www.amazon.com/GEEKHOM-Grilling-Resistant-Waterproof-Potholder/dp/B01KZBY806?tag=w050b-20" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank" data-aps-asin="B01KZBY806" data-aps-asc-tag="w050b-20">Heat-resistant gloves for $20</a>:</strong> That cast iron gets <em>extremely</em> hot, so you&#x27;ll also need a good pair of mitts. (Even these won&#x27;t protect your hands for long, so you&#x27;ll need a place near the oven to set the pan down.)</p><p><strong><a data-offer-url="https://ooni.com/products/ooni-firestarters" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">Fire starters for $20</a>:</strong> If you&#x27;ve ever been intimidated by the idea of cooking with wood, don&#x27;t be! These fire starters make it quick and simple. Just light the end with a match, drop it in the fuel tray, and line up <a data-offer-url="https://ooni.com/products/ooni-premium-hardwood-5-oak-logs-2-pack" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">a few oak sticks</a> on top. Be sure to keep your wood dry if you don&#x27;t want to create a smoke stack in your backyard.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="GridWrapper-cFSKbf kfCuhH grid
